newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-French bosses back pro-reform union on dole fund.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French bosses back pro-reform union on dole fund.

text.p: France's industry leaders voted on Monday to team up with CFDT labour union leader Nicole Notat in running the country's unemployment benefit fund, at the expense of a far more virulent critic of the centre-right government.

The national employers federation (CNPF) said in a statement after a secret ballot that it was supporting Notat, whose union is pro-Socialist but backs the controversial welfare reforms set in motion by Prime Minister Alain Juppe last year.

The vote secures Notat the job of managing the strategically important unemployment fund along with the employers and further isolates rival contender Marc Blondel, leader of Force Ouvriere (FO) union, during a traditionally restive period for the labour movement in France.

Force Ouvriere spearheaded a crippling public sector strike last year against Juppe's plans to rein in welfare spending and Blondel himself rarely minces his words when it comes to taking a stab at Juppe or the government's economic and social policy.
Before the casting vote by employers on Monday, Blondel said the result was sure to go Notat's way because of pressure on business leaders from Juppe's Matignon office.
"There's so much political pressure this time, especially from Matignon, that the employers have had to put it to a secret ballot as a way out," Blondel told French radio.
The CNPF said it would not reveal the breakdown of the vote in the interests of maintaining the culture of contracutual dealings with the unions.

While the impact on industrial relations in France may take some time to unfold, the victory for Notat gives the pre-reform CFDT union a say over yet another of the country's strategically important funds, very much at Blondel's cost.

In July, Notat's pro-reform CFDT union ousted Blondel from another strategic role at the head of the public health insurance fund, the Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie, a post of power and patronage which the FO had held for 30 years.

Nonetheless, Notat has made it clear she does not share the exact same priorities as the employers who are campaigning for a cut in the payroll contributions which are the life source of the UNEDIC unemployment fund.
"We will not be bought off," Notat was quoted as saying in one newspaper on Monday. The unnemployed should be the first to benefit from any surplus in the fund, she said.
The UNEDIC fund expects to pull out of the red in 1996 with a surplus of 12 billion French francs ($2.3 billion) after runnning heavily into debt in the early 1990s.

The CNPF decision comes the same day as a strike by teachers against cuts of 2,300 in civil service education staff levels next year under the centre-right government's 1997 spending-cut budget and regional protests by rail workers over jobs.

The autumn period when people return to work and school is traditionally a time of labour unrest but there are few signs for the moment of the kind of conflict or union cohesion behind a crippling 24-day strike last November and December. ($1=5.170 French Franc)
